name: Little Elephant and Interval
description: The Little Elephant very much loves sums on intervals. This time he has a pair of integers l and r ( l ≤ r ) . The Little Elephant has to find the number of such integers x ( l ≤ x ≤ r ) , that the first digit of integer x equals the last one (in decimal notation). For example, such numbers as 101 , 477474 or 9 will be included in the answer and 47 , 253 or 1020 will not. Help him and count the number of described numbers x for a given pair l and r .
input_specification: The single line contains a pair of integers l and r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ 10 18 ) — the boundaries of the interval. Please, do not use the %lld specifier to read or write 64-bit integers in С++. It is preferred to use cin , cout streams or the %I64d specifier.
output_specification: On a single line print a single integer — the answer to the problem.
approach_summary: Express count as f(R) - f(L-1). Define memoized state dp[pos][tight][leading_zeros][cond] scanning digits from most to least significant in O(digits × base × states).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 204A — Little Elephant and Interval [439. Digit DP]
topic_editorial.summary: Digit DP counting values in range $[L, R]$.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Counting valid integers in range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into $f(R) - f(L-1)$, where $f(X)$ counts valid integers in $[0, X]$. Numbers $\le X$ can be formed digit-by-digit from the most significant position. The constraint that the prefix does not exceed $X$ is tracked by a single boolean flag `tight`.
